literal: The strength of those who endure is the enduring of hunger; (it is) behind the strength of those who relieve that hunger.
translation: The strength of the strong is their ability to endure hunger, but it comes second to the strength of those who relieve the hunger of others.
modern: பசியைப் பொறுத்துக்கொள்ளும் ஆற்றல் பெரியதுதான்; ஆனால் அது, மற்றவர்களின் பசியைப் போக்கும் கொடையாளர்களின் ஆற்றலுக்குப் பின்னால் தான் நிற்கும்.
explanation: This couplet compares two kinds of strength: the personal discipline to endure hunger, and the generosity to feed the hungry. The word 'ஆற்றுவார்' refers to those who have the power to withstand hardships. While enduring one's own hunger ('பசி ஆற்றல்') is a great strength, the poet places it 'behind' ('பின்') the strength of those who relieve ('மாற்றுவார்') the hunger of others. In this chapter on giving, this highlights that the act of sharing food is a far greater virtue than personal self-denial.
